cases.question: Our barn roof is pitched at about 45°. Is that within range for RP-1?
cited_texts:
## Specifications

| Parameter | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Material | Aluminium rails, anodised |
| Coating thickness | 15 µm anodic layer |
| Fasteners and hooks | Stainless steel A2 |
| Corrosivity category | C3 |
| Roof slope | 10° to 60° |
| Maximum wind speed | 30 m/s |
| Maximum snow load | 3.0 kN/m² |

## Maximum values per product

| Product | Maximum wind speed | Maximum snow load |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GroundFrame GF-1 | 32 m/s | 2.4 kN/m² |
| GroundFrame GF-2 | 36 m/s | 3.5 kN/m² |
| RoofFlat RF-1 | 28 m/s | 2.0 kN/m² |
| RoofFlat RF-2 | 30 m/s | 2.4 kN/m² |
| RoofPitch RP-1 | 30 m/s | 3.0 kN/m² |
| CarportFrame CP-1 | 30 m/s | 2.4 kN/m² |

The maximum wind speed is the basic wind velocity from EN 1991-1-4. The maximum snow load is the characteristic snow load on the ground.
cases.answer: Yes, the roofPitch RP-1 is suitable for roofs with a slope of 10° to 60°, and a 45° slope is within this range.

cases.question: Which fasteners does RF-2 use, and why those?
cited_texts:
## Stainless steel fasteners

Aluminium systems use stainless steel fasteners:

- A2 stainless steel is used in systems rated up to C3.
- A4 stainless steel is used in systems rated C4 and above, because it resists chlorides from salt better.

## Specifications

| Parameter | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Material | Aluminium, anodised |
| Coating thickness | 20 µm anodic layer |
| Fasteners | Stainless steel A4 |
| Corrosivity category | C4 |
| Tilt angle | 10° |
| Maximum wind speed | 30 m/s |
| Maximum snow load | 2.4 kN/m² |
| Added roof load | 12 to 20 kg/m², including ballast |
| Maximum roof slope | 5° |
cases.answer: RF-2 uses stainless steel A4 fasteners because it is rated for C4 and A4 stainless steel resists chlorides from salt better.
